Theme

Latin word

condiciō

condiciō, condiciōnis f.

noun, third declension

a term of an agreement; terms; condition, terms; an offer, terms proposed; a proposal, the terms offered; a marriage proposal, a match; position, lot, circumstances

In this lexicon

  • agreement

    also used · classical · Traupman 295; Phaedr. 3.13.12: apibus condiciō placet

  • condition

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Arch. 25: sed eā condiciōne, nē quid posteā scrīberet; Phaedr. 3.13.12: apibus condiciō placet

  • offer

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.42.2: nōn respuit condiciōnem Caesar; M-O s.v. deal, terms (of agreement), settlement offer

  • propose

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 7.14.1: probāta condiciō est

  • propose

    also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 237: tū condiciōnem hanc accipe; Plaut. Trin. 501: condiciōnem quojus modī

  • situation

    also used · classical · Cic. Planc. 11: est haec condiciō līberōrum populōrum (Lewis & Short)

  • condiciō probātiōnis: test condition

    our formation

Examples

  • fūcī recūsant: apibus condiciō placet

    the drones refuse; the bees accept the termsPhaedr. 3.13.12

    In the entry for agreement

  • jubēre eī praemium tribuī, sed eā condiciōne, nē quid posteā scrīberet

    (we saw Sulla) order a reward to be given him, but on condition that he write nothing moreCic. Arch. 25

    In the entry for condition

  • vērum heus tū, hāc lēge tibi meam adstringō fidem: quae vēra audīvī taceō et contineō optumē

    but listen, I give you my word on this condition: what I hear that’s true, I keep to myself and hold in perfectlyTer. Eun. 102–103

    In the entry for condition
